subject.name: Biology
subject.description: Grade 11 Semester 1 Biology explores the molecular basis of life, the structure and function of cells, inheritance, and the applications of biotechnology through the lens of scientific inquiry. This course develops conceptual understanding of heredity, gene expression, and the biological systems that shape living organisms.

content.title: Unit 1 (Lo1)
content.description: This unit introduces genetic modification in biotechnology and explores how engineered organisms can improve agriculture, medicine, and industry while also raising ethical and ecological concerns.

concepts.title: Genetically modified organisms
concepts.description: This concept explains what genetically modified organisms are, how they are created, and why they are used in agriculture and biotechnology.

concepts.title: Beneficial characteristics
concepts.description: This concept highlights the useful traits introduced through genetic modification, such as improved productivity, disease resistance, and better food quality.

concepts.title: Unintended consequences for humans and ecosystems
concepts.description: This concept examines the possible risks of GMOs, including environmental disruption, biodiversity loss, and health or social concerns.

content.title: Unit 2 (Lo2)
content.description: This unit focuses on the molecular tools of genetic engineering, especially bacterial transformation, plasmids, and the relationship between genes and chromosomes.

concepts.title: Bacterial transformation technique
concepts.description: This concept explains how bacteria can take up foreign DNA and how this process is used to study and manipulate genetic traits.

concepts.title: Plasmids
concepts.description: This concept introduces plasmids as small circular DNA molecules that carry genes and function as useful vectors in biotechnology.

concepts.title: Genes and chromosomes (as a definition only)
concepts.description: This concept defines genes and chromosomes and clarifies their role as the basic units of hereditary information in living organisms.

concepts.title: Mitosis
concepts.description: This concept describes the process of mitosis and its importance in growth, repair, and maintaining genetic continuity.

content.title: Unit 3 (Lo3)
content.description: This unit explains the structure and function of DNA, the mechanism of DNA replication, and how genetic information flows through transcription and translation to produce proteins.

concepts.title: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA)
concepts.description: This concept defines DNA as the hereditary material that stores the information needed for growth, development, and reproduction.

concepts.title: Macromolecule with nucleotide subunits
concepts.description: This concept explains that DNA is a macromolecule made of nucleotide subunits, each containing a sugar, phosphate, and nitrogenous base.

concepts.title: Double helix and Complementary strands
concepts.description: This concept describes the double-helical structure of DNA and the pairing of complementary strands that ensures accurate genetic copying.

concepts.title: Sugar-phosphate backbone and nitrogenous bases
concepts.description: This concept identifies the sugar-phosphate backbone and the nitrogenous bases that carry genetic information and direct base pairing.

concepts.title: Nucleotide sequences
concepts.description: This concept highlights how the sequence of nucleotides determines the coded instructions for building proteins and regulating cell activities.

concepts.title: DNA replication by semiconservative template mechanism
concepts.description: This concept explains how DNA replicates by using each original strand as a template, producing two identical molecules.

concepts.title: Transcription and translation
concepts.description: This concept describes how genetic instructions are copied into RNA and then translated into proteins at the ribosome.

concepts.title: RNA types and structure
concepts.description: This concept compares the main types of RNA and explains how their structures support their roles in gene expression.

concepts.title: Protein Synthesis
concepts.description: This concept summarizes how DNA instructions are used to make proteins, which are essential for structure, function, and cell regulation.

content.title: Unit 4 (Lo4)
content.description: This unit explores genetic manipulation techniques used to create new combinations of traits, including DNA analysis, gene insertion methods, and transformation strategies in living cells.

concepts.title: Genetic manipulation for new combinations of traits
concepts.description: This concept explains how biotechnology can combine desirable traits by manipulating an organism’s DNA to produce new genetic combinations.

concepts.title: DNA electrophoresis
concepts.description: This concept explains how electrophoresis separates DNA fragments by size, helping scientists analyze genetic material and confirm successful modifications.

concepts.title: Steps in GMO
concepts.description: This concept outlines the key stages in creating a genetically modified organism and the logic behind each step in the process.

concepts.title: DNA constructs insertion
concepts.description: This concept describes how engineered DNA constructs are introduced into cells so that new traits can be expressed.

concepts.title: Shooting with gene gun
concepts.description: This concept introduces the gene gun method, a physical way to deliver DNA into target cells.

concepts.title: Bacterial transformation
concepts.description: This concept shows how bacteria can take up foreign DNA and be used as vehicles for recombinant gene delivery.

concepts.title: Viral delivery
concepts.description: This concept explores using viruses as delivery systems for introducing new genetic material into cells.

content.title: Unit 5 (Lo5)
content.description: This unit develops the foundations of classical genetics by examining alleles, inheritance patterns, and the use of Punnett squares to predict the outcomes of genetic crosses.

concepts.title: Distinguish between genes and alleles
concepts.description: This concept clarifies the difference between a gene and its alternative forms, called alleles, and why both are important in inheritance.

concepts.title: Use Punnett squares to predict outcomes of genetic crosses
concepts.description: This concept demonstrates how Punnett squares are used to predict the probability of genotypes and phenotypes in offspring.

concepts.title: Phenotypic and genotypic results (Heterozygote – Homozygote)
concepts.description: This concept explains how different allele combinations produce heterozygous or homozygous individuals and how these appear as observable traits.

concepts.title: Selective breeding
concepts.description: This concept shows how humans choose organisms with desirable traits to produce offspring with those characteristics over generations.

concepts.title: Gregor Mendel's contributions to our understanding of genetics
concepts.description: This concept introduces Mendel’s experiments and the laws that established the scientific basis of inheritance.

concepts.title: Patterns of inheritance
concepts.description: This concept explains the different ways characteristics are inherited and why some traits follow predictable patterns in families.

concepts.title: Simple dominance (Laws of simple dominance – first and second Mendelian laws)
concepts.description: This concept covers the first and second Mendelian laws and how dominant and recessive alleles determine trait expression.

concepts.title: Incomplete dominance
concepts.description: This concept explains inheritance in which heterozygous individuals show a blended phenotype rather than one dominant trait completely masking the other.

concepts.title: Codominance
concepts.description: This concept explains codominance, where two alleles are both expressed in the phenotype of a heterozygous organism.

content.title: Unit 6 (Lo6)
content.description: This unit links genetics to chromosomes and cell division by examining meiosis, crossing over, chromosome arrangements, and abnormal chromosomal changes.

concepts.title: Chromosomes and Genes
concepts.description: This concept explains how chromosomes carry genes and how their structure organizes hereditary information.

concepts.title: Mitosis
concepts.description: This concept reviews mitosis as the process that maintains chromosome number during growth and tissue repair.

concepts.title: Crossing over
concepts.description: This concept describes crossing over during meiosis, where chromosomes exchange segments and increase genetic variation.

concepts.title: Hybrid/Dihybrid crosses
concepts.description: This concept explores crosses involving two genes and how their inheritance patterns can be predicted and analyzed.

concepts.title: Karyotype
concepts.description: This concept shows how karyotypes are used to examine chromosome number and structure in individuals and diagnose chromosomal disorders.

concepts.title: Independent segregation
concepts.description: This concept explains Mendel’s law of independent assortment and how different genes are distributed during gamete formation.

concepts.title: Segregation and cross over
concepts.description: This concept connects segregation and crossing over to the generation of new combinations of inherited traits.

concepts.title: Abnormalities (chromosomal mutation)
concepts.description: This concept looks at chromosome abnormalities and how genetic or chromosomal mutations affect organismal development.

content.title: Unit 7 (Lo7)
content.description: This unit introduces genomics and the Human Genome Project, highlighting how DNA sequencing and genome analysis can improve health, biodiversity understanding, and future innovation.

concepts.title: Genomics
concepts.description: This concept explains genomics as the study of the complete set of genetic material in an organism and the insights it provides.

concepts.title: The Human Genome Project
concepts.description: This concept outlines the Human Genome Project and its role in mapping the human genome to improve medicine and biology.

concepts.title: Genomics and biodiversity, alternative energy, and human and animal health
concepts.description: This concept shows how genomic research contributes to biodiversity conservation, renewable energy, and improved health outcomes for humans and animals.

content.title: Midterm revisions
content.description: A focused review of the major ideas, subtopics, and skills covered in the first half of the semester to prepare students for assessment success.

content.title: Final revisions
content.description: This final review section reinforces the key concepts in genetics, molecular biology, and biotechnology before the end-of-course evaluation.

content.title: Other links
content.description: Additional biology videos and supporting study material that extend understanding beyond the core learning outcomes.
